tasks.message: After a separately authorized Start, inspect README.md at the assignment's pinned source and identify the best existing heading for a short Managed Sprint operation section. Return a read-only inventory of what is already documented and the missing explanation, without creating report files. Check these acceptance facts: one active Managed Sprint per canonical project; a launcher operation reserves the same project while pending, provisioning, prepared, Waiting, or running; parallel task nodes stay inside that one sprint; different already registered canonical projects remain independent. PROJECT_BUSY means inspect the owning operation and its truthful status, resume or stop only with the appropriate current grant, and wait for the existing engine's terminal and owned-resource cleanup proof before the slot is reused. Never suggest project aliases, deleting history, editing control storage, or manually removing leases. Manual autonomous_mode=false parks verified preparation as Waiting before task activation and needs an explicit authorized Start; true merely requests automatic activation and still requires current policy, start authority, and an available existing executor. Missing authority or infrastructure is a blocker, not success. The explicit envelope requires a boolean; absent legacy fields retain legacy dispatch. Record README's actual initial checksum and current source commit using read-only Git or standard-library checks. Missing prose is the expected input to the next edit, not a reason to fabricate a pass. Return DONE only for this completed analysis; use STOP or NEED_DECISION for a real provenance or authority blocker. For the read-only result, report no branch and the unchanged pinned source commit.

Explain: (1) one active Managed Sprint per canonical project, with the launcher reservation also covering pending/provisioning/prepared/manual Waiting operations; parallel nodes do not permit a second sprint or an alias, while different registered projects remain independent; (2) practical PROJECT_BUSY recovery: inspect the existing owner's status, use the same saved operation for an authorized retry/Start, or request an authorized stop, preserve results/logs/history, and wait for durable terminal plus owned process/lease cleanup proof before retrying a genuinely new launch; a stop request alone is not proof of Stopped; (3) autonomous_mode=false means prepared Waiting without execution until explicit Start with current authority; autonomous_mode=true is only a request and must pass current operator policy, start permission, and availability of the existing agent client. Treat PUBLICATION_REQUIRED, EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE, and missing grants as explicit recoverable blockers, not permission to bypass checks. State that the explicit launcher envelope requires a boolean and old legacy JSON with absent new fields keeps its original dispatch. Include a small manual-versus-automatic comparison and an ordered PROJECT_BUSY recovery checklist. Do not invent undocumented command syntax, URLs, administrator grants, source-update permission, or successful external demonstrations. Keep all changes in README.md; do not change engine code, schemas, tests, secrets, configuration, or introduce a model client or scheduler. Run isolated automated documentation checks in this same write assignment: git diff --check; assert the changed tracked path set is exactly README.md; use a temporary standard-library-only check to confirm the new section covers PROJECT_BUSY, autonomous_mode=false and true, canonical-project exclusivity, preservation of history, and authorized Start. Record each actual command, exit status, concise output, and the exact final result commit. These are documentation checks, not proof of runtime, Telegram, mobile, tunnel, or PR acceptance. Keep unavailable external evidence explicitly NOT_RUN/BLOCKED; completing this documentation work does not complete release acceptance. Commit only the README change on the assigned branch and submit the exact clean result through the existing engine; do not publish, merge, import another sprint, activate an application, or touch runtime state. Both independent reviewer gates must inspect that exact result. Perform the final check here, before this result goes directly to the terminal, because the manifest pins the original README checksum and a later successor cannot silently treat the edited checksum as equivalent. If a future assignment or rework is blocked by checksum/provenance drift, preserve evidence and route to the Coordinator for explicit existing recovery; never invent a replacement checksum or bypass preflight.
